analysis: Both units are base-side text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 920-1543). No patch or head text was supplied, so the actual diff is not visible; this is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. The file is documentation only, with no executable code. The base content describes security-relevant behavior that a later pass should check against any head or patch changes. (1) `darkbloom unenroll` (lines 1204-1221): the App Attest keep-serving option requires macOS 27+ and fresh coordinator approval, with no fallback to cleanup; privilege escalation is limited to a fixed, read-only profile inventory command (TB-011, T-057). (2) Prefix-cache and SSD settings (lines 1448-1467): SSD caching is on by default, the kill switch is DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE, and the TTL and disk-budget environment variables are forwarded to the daemon. This ties to T-041 and SEC-035, whose sign-off sets the 30-minute TTL cap and the available-disk/2 budget. Any doc change to those values should be checked against T-041. (3) `darkbloom report` (lines 1252-1300): uploads are explicit, log privacy redaction is preserved, device-wide DeviceCheck observations are labeled not attributable, and key identifiers and paths are dropped (T-058). (4) Model cache location is read from provider.toml only; ambient Hugging Face and XDG variables are not honored (lines 941-979). (5) Update verification of bundle, binary and metallib hashes (lines 1092-1093) relates to T-013 and T-034. (6) The device token and local-mode token files are 0600 (lines 1324-1325). No inconsistencies with the canonical threat model were observed in the visible base text. If a later pass sees a diff, check it against T-041, T-057 and T-058, and against the SEC-035 TTL cap.
